statement: You are given an integer n. Return true if n is odd and false if it is even.

Do it with a bit test instead of the % operator: the lowest bit of an integer is 1 exactly when the integer is odd, so the answer is whether n & 1 equals 1. In two's complement this also holds for negative numbers.

examples.explanation: 13 is 1101 in binary. Its lowest bit is 1, so 13 & 1 = 1 and 13 is odd.
8 is 1000 in binary. Its lowest bit is 0, so 8 & 1 = 0 and 8 is even.
